D005-D006_h001.question:
For the last couple of months, it’s like my life has split in two.

About eight weeks ago, I started hearing this woman’s voice, clear as day, like she’s standing right behind me. She comments on what I’m doing, sometimes whispers my name, sometimes tells me how talented and special I am. Around the same time, I became absolutely convinced this casting director I met once is secretly in love with me. I “see” signs everywhere—her posts, movie posters, even subway ads—that I’m sure are coded messages from her. I’ve tried DM’ing her, even showing up near her office, because I feel we’re meant to be together.

Most of these two months I’ve been on this insane high—sleeping maybe three hours a night, full of energy, talking nonstop, writing screenplays, feeling like I’m destined to be huge. Money’s been flying out of my account on headshots, classes, Ubers, like it doesn’t matter.

But there was this stretch—maybe two, three weeks—where that high dropped off. I wasn’t amped up or wired anymore, just sort of flat and tired. Even then, the voice kept going, and I still “knew” she loved me. The beliefs and the voice never really let up, even when my mood did.
D005-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h002.question:
For about two months now, I’ve been convinced that people are tracking me. It started with this idea that my laptop camera was on even when the light wasn’t, and then it spread—I feel like there are cameras in the hallway, in the coffee shop where I write, even in my apartment ceiling. I’m sure someone’s collecting material from my drafts and emails to use against me. I know it sounds unreasonable, but it feels absolutely real in the moment.

Around the same time, my energy just exploded. I barely slept—maybe two or three hours a night—but I didn’t feel tired. I was writing nonstop, firing off pitches at 3 a.m., talking faster than people could keep up. My thoughts race; I jump from idea to idea and feel like my brain is “lit up.” That amped-up feeling has been there for most of this whole stretch.

There was a stretch of a couple of weeks, though, where the paranoia and seeing shadowy figures in doorways and in my room at night kept going even after that “high” energy dropped off and my mood felt more flat. The sense of being watched never really let up.
D005-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h003.question:

I feel it physically sometimes: like tiny bugs crawling on my arms or someone brushing past me when no one’s there. That’s been continuous for these two months.

There was a stretch, maybe three weeks in the middle, when the “high” dropped off—I wasn’t euphoric or driven, just flat and scared—but the sense of being monitored and the crawling sensations didn’t let up at all.

D005-D006_h007.question:

I’m convinced my organs are rotting or rearranging themselves, even though scans and tests keep coming back normal. My motivation for everyday stuff is gone, though. I skip showers, forget meals, can’t make myself answer emails or meet deadlines, even when I’m wired and full of ideas.

There was a stretch of a few weeks when the “high” dropped out completely—I felt flat and not especially up or down—but the belief about my body being ruined stayed just as strong. Sometimes I even find myself copying other people’s gestures without meaning to, like my body just echoes what they do.
D005-D006_h007.options:

It started about three months ago. On my night shifts, I became convinced something terrible was happening, like the world was rotting from the inside out. I’d look at the conveyor belt and think, “Why am I even doing this if everything’s about to collapse?” It doesn’t feel like a thought; it feels like a certainty that everything is about to end.

Around the same time, I started hearing voices, like a couple of people standing just behind me, talking about how pointless it all is, or telling me to pay attention because “the end is close.” I know nobody’s there, but it sounds as clear as my coworkers. Sometimes my face kind of twists up or I make these weird expressions without meaning to—people at work have asked what’s wrong when I didn’t even realize I was doing it.

For most of these three months I’ve also been on this wired high—sleeping maybe two hours after shift, feeling like I don’t need rest, talking fast, taking on extra work, thinking I can fix everything before the “collapse.” But there was a stretch, maybe a couple of weeks, where that energy just dropped. I wasn’t revved up or anything, but the voices and the belief that everything was ending just kept going, like they had a life of their own separate from my mood.
D005-D006_h024.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D006_h025.question:
I’m a social worker, so I’m used to listening more than talking, but lately it’s been hard to explain what’s happening. For about three months now, I’ve been convinced there’s something terribly wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting or crawling. Tests keep coming back normal, but I’m sure the doctors are missing something. Sometimes I can actually feel things moving under my skin, like bugs or wires shifting, even when I can see there’s nothing there.

Most of this time I’ve also been “revved up.” I sleep maybe two or three hours and still feel wired. My mind races with ideas about new programs I could start at work, and I talk so fast my coworkers can’t keep up. I’ve spent money we really don’t have on supplies and donations because I feel like I’m on some kind of mission.

But there was a stretch—at least a couple of weeks—where that high energy dropped off. I wasn’t overly happy or energized, just flat, and those beliefs about my body and the crawling sensations didn’t let up. Sometimes in those periods I just stop talking altogether at home or at work, even though I know I could if I tried.
D005-D006_h025.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
